subject: Mathematics
title: Completing the square and the discriminant
explanation: Completing the square writes a quadratic in the form (x + p)² + q. For x² + bx + c, p is half of b: x² + bx + c = (x + b/2)² − (b/2)² + c.
This form shows the turning point straight away. Because (x + p)² is never negative, y = (x + p)² + q has a minimum value of q, when x = −p. The turning point is (−p, q).
If the x² term has a number a in front, take a out of the x terms first: 2x² + 12x + 7 = 2(x² + 6x) + 7 = 2(x + 3)² − 18 + 7 = 2(x + 3)² − 11.
The discriminant of ax² + bx + c = 0 is b² − 4ac. If it is positive there are two different real roots; if it is 0 there is one repeated (equal) root; if it is negative there are no real roots.

A line and a curve: set the two expressions for y equal and rearrange to a quadratic = 0. The line is a tangent when b² − 4ac = 0, cuts the curve twice when b² − 4ac > 0 and misses it when b² − 4ac < 0.
Quadratic inequalities: find the roots, sketch the U-shaped graph, then read off where it is above (> 0) or below (< 0) the x-axis.
keyPoints: Turning point of (x + p)² + q is (−p, q).
b² − 4ac > 0: two roots; = 0: equal roots; < 0: none.

examples.q: Write x² − 8x + 21 in the form (x + p)² + q and state its minimum value.
steps: Half of −8 is −4, so start with (x − 4)² = x² − 8x + 16.
The minimum value is 5, when x = 4.

examples.q: Find the values of k for which x² + kx + 9 = 0 has equal roots.

practice.q: x² + 6x + 2 is written in the form (x + p)² + q. Find p.
practice.hint: p is half of the number in front of x.

practice.q: x² + 6x + 2 is written in the form (x + p)² + q. Find q.
practice.hint: (x + 3)² = x² + 6x + 9. How much must you add to 9 to get 2?

practice.q: Find the minimum value of y = x² − 10x + 30.
practice.solution: x² − 10x + 30 = (x − 5)² + 5. A square is never negative, so the minimum value is 5.

practice.q: Find the x-coordinate of the turning point of y = x² + 4x − 1.
practice.hint: Write it as (x + 2)² + q. The turning point is where the bracket is 0.
practice.solution: x² + 4x − 1 = (x + 2)² − 5, so the turning point is at x = −2.

practice.q: 2x² + 12x + 7 is written in the form 2(x + 3)² + q. Find q.
Find the value of the discriminant b² − 4ac for 2x² + 5x − 3 = 0.
How many real roots does x² − 4x + 4 = 0 have?
practice.solution: b² − 4ac = 16 − 16 = 0, so there is one repeated root (x = 2).

practice.q: How many real roots does 3x² − 2x + 1 = 0 have?
practice.solution: b² − 4ac = 4 − 12 = −8, which is negative, so there are no real roots.

practice.q: x² + kx + 16 = 0 has equal roots. Find the positive value of k.
The line y = 3x + k is a tangent to the curve y = x² + 1. Find k.
practice.hint: Set x² + 1 = 3x + k, write it as a quadratic = 0, and use b² − 4ac = 0.
practice.solution: x² − 3x + (1 − k) = 0. For a tangent, 9 − 4(1 − k) = 0, so 4k = −5 and k = −1.25.

practice.hint: Factorise to find where the curve cuts the x-axis, then think about where it is below the axis.
practice.solution: (x − 3)(x + 2) < 0. The graph is a U shape, below the axis between the roots: −2 < x < 3.

practice.q: For which values of k does x² + 2x + k = 0 have two different real roots?
practice.hint: Two different real roots means b² − 4ac > 0.

practice.q: x² − 6x + c = 0 has no real roots. Find the smallest whole number c can be.
practice.solution: 36 − 4c < 0, so c > 9. The smallest whole number is 10.
